strings.MZB_USA_eastern_african_developments_des:
The aim of the temporary OFN Mandates in Africa is to serve as transition between German rule and local sovereignty.

If we manage to peacefully carry out our decolonization plans, we will be able to bring back 80% of the resources we have generated here.

If we choose to prematurely decolonize, we will only be able to bring back 40% of the resources we have generated here.

In the case of a complete collapse of the mandate, we will we will have to abandon the resources we have generated here.
strings.MZB_USA_William_R_Peers_hog_desc:
Head of Government
Colonial Government
--------------
Once, in the boardrooms of Washington years prior, the African Mandates were a lofty proposal: OFN-aligned African republics, free and democratic. Such intentions were discarded long ago, but William R. Peers remains. He is determined to let this nation fall no further.

The task before him is not easy. The hardliners resent and obstruct him, and the Africans treat him no differently than any other general. But his goal was never praise. It is simply to try to prevent this tragedy from taking any more lives than it has to. God willing, this African debacle will be a mere blemish on America's foreign policy, and not a scar.
strings.MZB_USA_Kenneth_Rush_for_desc:
Foreign Minister
Colonial Government
--------------
Kenneth Rush, former president of Union Carbide turned chief diplomat for the African Mandates, is perhaps the last optimist in the whole of Africa. Resolute in his belief that peace can prevail, the executive drives towards a diplomatic solution, as thousands fear the worst.

To most, his confidence is misplaced. Rush has managed to cut some impressive deals, but the Republic's grip loosens faster every day. Still, that endless confidence within Mr. Rush is a faint glimmer of hope in a moment of crisis. One person seems to believe in the version of the CAR that Washington is selling. Can it really all be lies?
strings.MZB_USA_Paul_Nitze_eco_desc:
Economy Minister
Colonial Government
--------------
Paul Nitze, one of the first figures to imagine the scale of the Cold War, sits at the helm of one of its greatest creations. Now, he has been given a new challenge: To turn this war-ravaged wreck into a meaningful asset for the OFN. This will be his hardest yet.

For his part, Nitze's approach is highly... unitary. The general views his assignment as one of strengthening the OFN and weakening its foes, and Nitze has brought in fleets of American companies to ensure the US leaves the CAR stronger than it arrived. With any luck, Africa's natural resources will be the fuel that draws the Cold War to a close - even if the Republic burns away in the process.
strings.MZB_USA_Paul_D_Harkins_sec_desc:
Security Minister
Colonial Government
--------------
“Sure, we took a big hit in 1945 - a sucker punch. But in South Africa, we got up and hit back hard - damn hard! That's a sign, you know. We showed the world that if those brownshirts and blackshirts try something, we can take 'em! But if we can beat back those Nazis, and we can beat back those Nazis, we sure as hell can beat back some warlord who claims it's his birthright to rule every Tom, Dick, and Larry in his sight! So I'm telling you all, if there's some far-flung thug who wants to get with Japan, we're marching down there! We're gonna teach them a thing or two, or my name isn't Paul D. Harkins!”

“so...what's your plan, exactly?”
strings.MZB_USA_Legacy_Ostafrikaner_Research_des: When we marched across the tropical hell of Hüttig's lands, we found more than just violent death, disease, and human suffering. In the depths of his cruel laboratories, we found stockpiles of chemical weapons, and well-documented research on their production. This has given us a useful chemical industry in the few areas truly under our control, and the developments Hüttig made will assist the US military in their own research of this lethal science.
strings.MZB_USA_East_African_Warlordism_desc: In the brutality of Hüttig's kingdom, it was inevitable that some would find it unbearable and resist their captors. Most of these acts of resistance were cut short by an executioner's bullet, and only the most brutal and ruthless rebels have survived this long. Armed with a miscellany of stolen German and black market weapons, they have turned East Africa into a bloody patchwork of warlord states. We must act decisively to restore order from chaos.
strings.MZB_USA_Lackluster_Infrastructures_desc: Due to the instability of our mandate's interior, useful infrastructure is almost non-existent outside of the East African coast. German construction projects were mostly abandoned after Hüttig's frustration with constant sabotage and attacks on construction teams. This makes controlling anywhere more than a few miles from the coast an exercise in futility, at least until our own infrastructure projects make some headway where Hüttig failed.
strings.MZB_USA_okello_rebellion: The situation in Tanganyika has spiralled out of control!
